---
title: "Functions, formats and rounding"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

```{r setup}
library(sasonr)
```

sasonr implements SAS functions, formats and informats in R with SAS
semantics: missing values, fixed-length character results, result lengths
and `_ERROR_` diagnostics follow SAS 9.4. Every function has a reference page
(see [Reference](../reference/index.html)) with the SAS syntax, the
differences from base R and its verification status.

## Calling SAS functions inside a DATA step

```{r}
res <- sas_run("
data _null_;
  s = 'a,b,,c';
  w2 = scan(s, 2, ',');
  wl = scan(s, -1, ',');
  c  = compress('A-1 B-2', '-', 's');
  x  = catx('/', 'a', ' ', 'b');
  d  = intnx('month', '15MAR2026'd, 1, 'e');
  put w2= wl= c= x= d= date9.;
run;
")
res$log
```

## Calling them from R

The implementations are exported as `sas_f_<name>()`, so translated code can
run on its own and you can use them directly:

```{r}
sas_f_round(2.675, 0.01)
sas_f_scan("a b c", 2)
```

## Rounding

SAS rounding differs from base R in ways that matter for clinical tables:

| Situation | SAS | base R |
|---|---|---|
| `ROUND(x, unit)` on halves | away from zero | half to even (`round(0.5) == 0`) |
| values just below a half in binary (e.g. 1.005, 2.675) | rounded up: `ROUND` applies a small relative fuzz | rounded down |
| `w.d` formats | rounding with a much smaller tolerance than `ROUND` | `sprintf()` uses the binary value |
| negative values that round to zero | `ROUND` then `put` shows `0.00` | `-0.00` is possible |

```{r}
x <- c(1.005, 2.675, 23 / 80 * 100)
round(x, c(2, 2, 1))              # base R
sas_f_round(x, c(0.01, 0.01, 0.1)) # SAS ROUND
```

sasonr is checked against about 21,000 rounding points generated by SAS
9.4. Points that are not yet reproduced exactly (a few edge windows of the
fuzz, very narrow `BEST` widths) stop with `sasonr_unsupported` instead of
returning a possibly different value. See
[Conformance status](conformance.html) for the current numbers.
